 Order

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 27.01.2022 passed by MACT, Jobat, district Alirajpur in Claim Case No.124/2022 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the death of Mukamsingh, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.12,05,500/-
along with interest.

The breakup of the compensation amount is as under:
 HEAD AMOUNT  Loss of dependency -Rs.10,12,500/-
(i.e.Rs.6000 1500 FP - 1/4 PE =5,625 x 12 x 15 (M)) Consortium -Rs.1,60,000/-

Funeral expenses -Rs.16,500/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.16,500/-
 --------------------

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
He further submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not assessing minimum wages towards income of the deceased.
Hence, prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents has argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
Smt. Kamla vs Chetanya on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6161098/
2 6.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.

Considering the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and the evidence that has come on record, in the considered opinion of this court, the just and proper amount of monthly income of the deceased in the present case would be Rs.7,000/- per month considering the minimum wages prevalent on the relevant period.

Hence, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be modified as under:
 HEAD AMOUNT  Loss of dependency -Rs.11,81,340/-
 (i.e. Rs.7000 25% FP - 1/4 PE x 12 x 15 (M))
 Consortium -Rs.1,60,000/-

Funeral expenses -Rs.16,500/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.16,500/-
 -------------------
. Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.13,74,340/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.12,05,500/-.
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.1,68,840/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
8. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.1,68,840/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
